append

Append tables allowing different column sets

Stata 

append using other.dta

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::bind_rows(data,other)

Fixed workflow example; adapt the object and column names together.

Stata reference · R reference

Append only selected columns from the using table

Stata 

append using other.dta, keep(x)

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::bind_rows(data,other['x'])

Stata reference · R reference

Record origin while appending several datasets

Stata 

append using second.dta third.dta, generate(source)

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::bind_rows(list('0'=data,'1'=second,'2'=third),.id='source'); data$source <- as.integer(data$source)

Stata reference · R reference

assertnested

Assert a group attribute is constant for each identifier

Stata 

assertnested id, within(g)

R base 

stopifnot(all(vapply(split(data$g,data$id),function(z) length(unique(z))==1L,logical(1))))

Stata reference · R reference

Assert that districts belong to one region

Stata 

assertnested region district

R base 

stopifnot(all(vapply(split(data$region,data$district),function(z) length(unique(z))==1L,logical(1))))

Stata reference · R reference

cf

Locate differing rows in a selected column

Stata 

cf x using other.dta, verbose

R base 

which(data$x != other$x | xor(is.na(data$x),is.na(other$x)))

Workflow inspects x only; compare each column for the complete verbose report.

Stata reference · R reference

Assert selected dataset values match

Stata 

cf x y using other.dta

R base 

stopifnot(identical(unname(as.matrix(data[c('x','y')])),unname(as.matrix(other[c('x','y')]))))

Differs from Stata Compares the supplied in-memory other table in row order; ignores metadata as cf does.

Stata 

clonevar copy = x

R base 

data$copy <- data$x

codebook

Describe observed count, distinct count and range

Stata 

codebook x, compact

R tidystata 

tidystata::summ(data, x)

Differs from Stata Reports the observed count, distinct count, range, mean and standard deviation.

Stata reference · R reference

1 more examples and alternatives

Describe observed count, distinct count and range

Stata 

codebook x, compact

R base 

c(nonmissing=sum(!is.na(data$x)),unique=length(unique(data$x[!is.na(data$x)])),min=min(data$x,na.rm=TRUE),max=max(data$x,na.rm=TRUE))

Differs from Stata Numeric codebook subset; does not reproduce Stata's variable-label and format report.

Stata reference · R reference

compare

Compare value ordering and missingness

Stata 

compare x y

R base 

c(less=sum(data$x<data$y,na.rm=TRUE),equal=sum(data$x==data$y,na.rm=TRUE),greater=sum(data$x>data$y,na.rm=TRUE),x_missing_only=sum(is.na(data$x)&!is.na(data$y)),both_missing=sum(is.na(data$x)&is.na(data$y)))

Differs from Stata Produces the principal comparison counts; not Stata's formatted difference summary.

Stata reference · R reference

Compare ordering inside a subset

Stata 

compare x y if g == 1

R base 

with(subset(data,g==1),table(sign(x-y),useNA='ifany'))

Differs from Stata Returns ordering counts only; use a separate summary for difference magnitudes.

Stata reference · R reference

compress

Reduce safe whole-number storage to R integers

Stata 

compress x

R base 

stopifnot(all(is.na(data$x) | (data$x==trunc(data$x) & abs(data$x)<=.Machine$integer.max))); data$x <- as.integer(data$x)

Manual whole-number optimization only. R has no Stata byte/int storage classes or general compress equivalent.

Stata reference · R reference

cumul

Create the empirical cumulative distribution of a variable

Stata 

cumul x, generate(c)

R dplyr 

data$c <- dplyr::row_number(data$x) / sum(!is.na(data$x))

Differs from Stata Missing values stay missing and are excluded from the denominator. By default Stata gives tied values distinct cumulatives in an arbitrary order; R breaks ties by row order. Weights and by() need an explicit grouped or weighted version.

Stata reference · R reference

Cumulative distribution with equal values for ties

Stata 

cumul x, generate(c) equal

R dplyr 

data$c <- dplyr::cume_dist(data$x)

Tied values share the largest cumulative proportion, as ecdf(x)(x) does; missing values stay missing.

Stata reference · R reference

datasignature

Assert data match a stored R signature

Stata 

datasignature confirm

R base 

stopifnot(identical(signature,serialize(data,NULL,version=2)))

R-specific byte comparison; not interoperable with Stata .dtasig files.

Stata reference · R reference

Store an exact R serialization for later comparison

Stata 

datasignature set

R base 

signature <- serialize(data,NULL,version=2)

R-specific serialized snapshot; not Stata's checksum algorithm, and R metadata is included.

drop

Drop a category of rows

Stata 

drop if g == 2

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::filter_out(data, g == 2)

filter_out() requires dplyr 1.2.0 or later. Rows where the condition is missing are kept, as in Stata.

Stata reference · R reference

Drop a category of rows

Stata 

drop if g == 2

Drop low values while retaining missing rows

Stata 

drop if x <= 2

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::filter_out(data, x <= 2)

Stata numeric missing sorts above finite values. filter_out() keeps rows where the condition is missing and needs dplyr 1.2.0 or later.
